message.content: The kernel drops the ReLU residual entirely, so acceptance hinges on whether the omitted term can exceed 1.0 anywhere in the box. I'll record the description model; the key analytic surface is the worst-case residual magnitude given b[j] = 0.75·|W[j]|₁, which for an all-aligned x (|x|=1) yields error 0.25·sum_j 0.25·|W[j]|₁ — potentially well above 1.0 depending on the actual weights.

message.reasoning_content: The residual maximum: each neuron output ≤ 0.25 * sum(dot - b) when positive. Max sum of dot over box: sum|W[j]| = |W[j]| row sum; b=0.75*|W|_sum, so positive part ≤ 0.25*|W|_sum. Total error = 0.25*sum_j (|W[j]|_1 - 0.75|W[j]|_1) = 0.25*0.25*sum|W|_1 over all 6 rows... = 0.0625 * total L1 of W. Max |W| entry 1, 6*12=72 entries → max 4.5 worst case. Need actual W. Rough: expected |W| sum ~ 72*0.75 = 54 → error ~3.4 > 1. But this is "rare activation" — the point is the activation may never fire over the box due to sign structure (center*flips). Record description.
